title: Crushing the Serpent Under the Heel
narrative: Nine days after four Salvadoran aviation technicians went missing in Santo, nobody has publicly identified the burned remains handed over on Saturday. A person familiar with the matter told the Washington Post it is "fairly certain" that at least some are not the Salvadorans'; the remains of roughly three bodies were "almost fused together," and DNA testing is being done outside Haiti. Bukele has posted nothing since Sunday night, and El Salvador's Diario El Mundo says his government has given no new information. Haiti's government has still said nothing, notes Jake Johnston of the Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR).

Meanwhile the planes keep coming. The Miami Herald counts at least a dozen flights since Thursday; the Post says more than 500 Salvadoran special forces are in Haiti, and Johnston says at least 1,000 may come. Both Johnston and the Herald say Bukele wants some of them outside the Gang Suppression Force, under his own commander. "A multilateral force, a bilateral force, and a private force," Johnston wrote; later he said it is hard to imagine Bukele undermining the force unless some in the US government are working with him. The force itself said Monday that "pressure on criminal groups will continue."

The effort to crush the gangs went on along several fronts. Haitian police struck Bel-Air on Sunday night with explosive drones; police sources say several gang members were killed, and a resident says innocent people were hurt. On Monday Salvadoran troops and Haitian police worked in Bon Repos, offensives were reported in Marin and Lizon, armored vehicles were filmed in Kenscoff, and the police posted video of its BRI unit in Mirebalais. A Gonaïves station says the US helped deliver 33 armored vehicles to the force and the police; no one else has reported that.

The gangs keep talking. Lanmò San Jou of 400 Mawozo, who says the four died "by mistake" in Chen Mechan's area, sang and showed off diamond teeth on video and says he holds three police officers; the Herald's sources say his men backed Chen Mechan in the 18 October attack. César Moreno, citing one local, names former deputy Lemaire Pierre as the man arming Chen Mechan, and a journalists' network accuses the prime minister of a quiet deal with gang leaders, without giving evidence. A widely shared video of a raid on a gang house, shared as Salvadoran commandos in Haiti, is from Ecuador, Moreno says.

Next door, Dominican President Luis Abinader says he will not let the gangs come within 20 kilometers of the border. His foreign minister says about 2,181 international personnel are now in Haiti, with 5,500 the goal within three months.

feed.text: Flights carrying Salvadoran soldiers and equipment kept landing on Monday: at least a dozen since Thursday, at least two on Sunday, a chartered cargo flight Monday afternoon and a second expected that evening. El Salvador has not said how many it has sent, but the number had reached 450 by Saturday "with hundreds more expected." On Monday Salvadoran forces under the GSF banner and Haitian police ran a joint operation in the Bon Repos area. "Bukele is reportedly seeking to deploy more troops to bolster the force and to operate independently of the mission, answering directly to his commander on the ground in Haiti." Sources told the paper that 400 Mawozo backed up Chen Mechan's gunmen in the 18 Oct attack. Lanmò San Jou also says he holds three Haitian police officers and showed a video of them criticizing the government for caring more about the Salvadorans than about them.
feed.evidence: named reporter; flight arrivals as she reports them; sources for the 400 Mawozo role and for Bukele's plan not named; the paper says it could not check that the three men are police
feed.other: Jake Johnston posted the same point about troops outside the GSF at 21:39 without giving a source.

feed.text: Posts video he says shows armored vehicles deployed in the commune of Kenscoff (he places it west of Port-au-Prince) and says the presence of the GSF, the Haitian police and "united countries" keeps growing.
feed.evidence: video, 16 seconds; no named source; no date or place shown that we can check

feed.text: "Even if @grok says it is Haiti, that is Ecuador. 98% of the news about Haiti is FALSE." He is answering a Dominican account (@Edwarda77427936, 18:30 on 26 Oct, about 138,000 views) whose video, it says, shows "an armed commando of Bukele's army" entering a house where Haitian gang members held three kidnapped foreigners, the gang members running and leaving their pistols behind.
feed.evidence: video, 37 seconds, with no date or place shown; neither account names a source
feed.other: Another source says: @MajewskiLove1 (01:00, 27 Oct) posted the same video in English as Salvadoran special forces in Haiti, "allegedly."

feed.text: Says that from November the group COMOGINDA plans demonstrations in Gonaïves (Artibonite) to demand operations against the armed gangs, and that, according to its sources, the group also questions what the GSF's real mission in Haiti is.
feed.evidence: station's sources, not named; not yet reported by others

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Haiti analyst at CEPR, author of "Aid State"
feed.text: Replying to the UN-focused outlet PassBlue, which wrote that the US plan for the GSF is not going well: "Hard to imagine Bukele is going to undermine the GSF unless he's coordinating with at least some in USG."
feed.evidence: his own judgment; no source given

feed.text: "BRI sou teren an nan Mibalè" (the BRI, the police search and intervention unit, on the ground in Mirebalais).
feed.evidence: official account; video, 17 seconds
feed.other: Radio Télé Confiance reported on 26 Oct that police special units had entered gang-held parts of Mirebalais.

feed.text: Says the Haitian police, together with the GSF, are stepping up offensives in Marin and Lizon in the Cul-de-Sac plain to push the gangs out and find the four Salvadorans.
feed.evidence: 2 photos; no named source
feed.other: Thériel Thélus said on 26 Oct that the Chen Mechan leader is hiding in Lizon; Radio Télé Confiance says he is at Marin 12.

feed.where: X, Haitian Creole and English, photo
feed.text: "Last night, Sunday, there was an exchange of gunfire between the Haitian National Police (PNH) and the vile gangs in the Bel Air area. According to a police source, several gang members were taken down during an operation in which the Task Force used drones to strike the gangs' positions."
feed.evidence: one police source, not named; 1 photo

feed.text: Says the Port-au-Prince Court of Appeal on Monday 26 Oct sent five defendants, including businessman Marc Antoine Acra, to trial before the criminal court without a jury on international drug trafficking charges in the 2015 Manzanares ship case (108 kg of cocaine and 15 kg of heroin found on board), and asked prosecutors to consider charging more people and companies involved in ordering, loading, shipping and unloading the sugar cargo. The station frames it as the vise tightening on the backers of the criminal economy now that operations against the foot soldiers are intensifying.
feed.evidence: station's own reporting ("according to our information"); no court document shown; not yet reported by others

feed.who: Presidency of the Dominican Republic, on President Luis Abinader's weekly press program (LA Semanal, Monday 26 Oct)
feed.text: Abinader: "We will act in coordination with the government of Haiti, but we will not allow those gangs within 20 kilometers of the border." He says the border is at its highest level of protection and the Dominican Republic is not at its moment of greatest risk. Defense Minister Lt. Gen. Carlos Antonio Fernández Onofre says the gangs control at least 70 percent of Port-au-Prince, people are moving mainly west rather than toward the border, at least two Haitian self-defense groups stand between the nearest gangs and the border, and intelligence shows no organized gangs in the north near Ouanaminthe (Juana Méndez). Foreign Minister Víctor "Ito" Bisonó says the Dominican Republic does not take part directly in operations, as a neighbor, but gives the GSF logistics: transit for contingents, medical evacuations, air permits, blood shipments and moving military cargo. It says about 2,181 international personnel are deployed, with a goal of about 5,500 within three months.
feed.evidence: on the record, named officials; official release
feed.other: Abinader posted it on X at 23:44 with 4 photos; Franklin Vargas (23:41) reported the 20-kilometer warning.

feed.who: Diario Libre (Dominican Republic), reporter Omar Santana
feed.text: Asked by Diario Libre founder Aníbal de Castro whether the four Salvadorans are alive, Abinader said: "I don't want to speculate, because we are talking about people and families," and that reports from Haiti show the Haitian authorities themselves do not know their status. He said the reinforcement of the border answers the possible effects of stepped-up operations after the attack, which has caused "indignation" among the force's member countries: "That indignation, I think, will help all those countries put more emphasis... on destroying and eliminating those gangs once and for all."
feed.evidence: on the record, named official answering a named journalist
feed.other: Franklin Vargas (00:11, 27 Oct) reports Abinader said he would receive Bukele if he wished to visit: "we would obviously receive him and give him all our support."
links: Franklin Vargas, Abinader on Bukele visit

feed.who: Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic (@luisabinader)
feed.text: "I identify with the position of President @NayibBukele, which we must support: defending the dignity and the life of those four Salvadorans..."
feed.evidence: on the record, signed post

feed.where: US daily (we read it in full through the DNYUZ reprint; the Post page is behind a paywall)
feed.text: A person familiar with the matter says it is "fairly certain" that at least some of the remains "were not those of the Salvadoran soldiers," which partly supports Bukele. The remains of roughly three bodies were "almost fused together," and DNA testing is being done outside Haiti. Says the four apparently lost their way on 18 Oct and escaped their burning SUV, per the Salvadoran military. Says Bukele has sent more than 500 special forces to join the search.
feed.evidence: one person, not named; named reporter
feed.other: Rolfy Martínez (00:16, 27 Oct) also says Bukele may have sent more than 500.

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Haiti analyst at CEPR, author of "Aid State"
feed.text: "Bukele apparently wants at least some of the Salvadoran troops deploying to Haiti to be *outside* of the GSF, with their own authorization. A multilateral force, a bilateral force, and a private force ... what could go wrong ..."
feed.evidence: no source given
feed.other: The Miami Herald (03:57, 27 Oct) reports the same, attributed to unnamed reporting.

feed.who: Dominican Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Mirex), reported by Franklin Vargas (@FranklinVargasG)
feed.text: The ministry says a post circulating on social media that has Bukele attacking the Dominican government and armed forces is false and comes from an account that does not exist, and that it is looking into where it came from, possibly for legal action.
feed.evidence: official statement as relayed; 1 photo
feed.other: A French-language account (@lemedia100filtr) had spread the attack as something Bukele "reportedly" said.

feed.text: Says citizens report a heavy GSF presence in Croix-des-Bouquets and that the gangs' presence has dropped somewhat in some sectors, though the situation is very unstable and clashes are reported at hot spots.
feed.evidence: video, 15 seconds; residents, not named

feed.text: Describes the three photos with the GSF statement: a convoy of eleven armored vehicles in an urban area, Chadian soldiers beside an armored vehicle, and a soldier in a Salvadoran helmet on a flight over the capital. Citing Radio Télé Galaxie and police sources, says several gang members were killed in Sunday night's police operation in Bel-Air. Says the Haitian army (FAd'H) held written tests on Sunday for about 2,000 recruits, from whom 700 will be picked, part of a plan to recruit 15,000 in three years.
feed.evidence: agency report; police sources not named

feed.who: Haitian Network of Anti-Corruption Journalists (RHAJAC), note signed by secretary general Djovany Michel; reported by EFE and Rezo Nodwes
feed.where: Haitian press group, French; Spanish agency story
feed.text: Urges Bukele to be careful in his operations in Haiti. Alleges a quiet understanding between Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé and gang leaders to keep himself in power, and protection for the gangs in political, business and police circles in Haiti and abroad; EFE adds that the note names the Haitian police high command and the Dominican police. Calls for independent inquiries into who funds and arms the gangs, and asks that people in gang-held areas not be treated as gang members.
feed.evidence: named group and signer; Rezo Nodwes says the note gives no evidence for the charges and carries no reply from those named

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Haiti analyst at CEPR, author of "Aid State"
feed.text: "Chartered cargo flights from El Salvador continue to arrive in Port-au-Prince. At least one yesterday and one today. 450 Salvadoran troops have reportedly already arrived and the expectation is at least a 1,000 may ultimately deploy. On paper, they are part of the GSF. But seems pretty clear Bukele and the GSF aren't exactly on the same page. Haitian government still hasn't said anything."
feed.evidence: 2 photos (flight listings); no named source for the 1,000
feed.other: Vant Bèf Info (20:27) relayed it in French, adding that the Haitian government has still not reacted publicly.

feed.text: Names Lemaire Pierre, a former deputy and candidate in Haiti, as "the real financier" behind the attack on the Salvadorans. "According to a local," Pierre gives arms and ammunition directly to Chen Mechan to spread terror in the plain, take control of 34 key neighborhoods and frighten voters into re-electing him.
feed.evidence: one local person, not named; photo of the man; not yet reported by others

feed.text: Video of residents of Delmas 33, driven from their homes by the gangs, saying they want to go back to their homes and neighborhood, which the gangs still hold.
feed.evidence: video, about 2 minutes 44 seconds, residents on camera

feed.who: Diario El Mundo (El Salvador), reporter Iliana Cornejo
feed.text: Timeline of the case. Says the four entered a gang-held area by mistake while using Google Maps to reach a supermarket, and that after an exchange of fire and air support, contact was lost. Says that nine days on, the Salvadoran government has announced no new action or information on their whereabouts.
feed.evidence: no source named for the Google Maps detail
feed.other: The Washington Post says they "apparently lost their way." El País quotes analyst Romain Le Cour: "No one has yet clarified why they were there."

feed.text: Posts video he says Lanmò San Jou put out singing a song and showing his diamond-covered teeth. Earlier (06:02, about 55,600 views) he posted video he says shows Lanmò being welcomed by people in his territory.
feed.evidence: videos, 26 seconds and about 87 seconds, gang leader on camera; no date or place shown
feed.other: Spanish-language outlets (z101digital, En el Foco RD, Punto y Coma, RD Somos Pueblo) ran his "by mistake" video all day, noting it does not prove the four are dead.

feed.who: Radio Télé Confiance (@RTConfiance), Haitian station, with journalist @jonphterdiplo
feed.where: X and YouTube, French and Creole
feed.text: Program headlined "Who is the brain behind the beheading of the Salvadoran soldiers in the Cul-de-Sac plain?" with a former member of the Léopards (an old Haitian army unit) making what it calls big revelations.
feed.evidence: video, about 4.5 minutes (not watched by us); the beheading is in the headline only; not yet reported by others
feed.other: No other source we read says the four were beheaded; the GSF and Bukele say the remains are not identified as theirs.

feed.text: As of Friday at least six aircraft, three Salvadoran and three American, had landed with about 100 elite troops. Romain Le Cour of the Global Initiative against Transnational Organized Crime: "Four Salvadoran soldiers were traveling on a Sunday at noon in an unescorted vehicle in an area controlled by gangs... No one has yet clarified why they were there"; "Residents have been describing a barrage of fire for nearly a week, and yet there has been no visible progress in the rescue"; Viv Ansanm "had shown signs of fragmentation" and the incident "could restore its cohesion." Crisis Group says a gang in Kenscoff recently killed dozens and kidnapped about 50. The Salvadoran government did not answer El País.
feed.evidence: named analyst and named organization quoted
links: Romain Le Cour on X, 26 Oct (his analysis for GEG; the GEG page not opened)

feed.text: "Following recent events involving personnel from the Salvadorian contingent, the #GSF reaffirms its determination to fulfil its mission in support of Haiti's security and stability. Pressure on criminal groups will continue, and their acts of violence will not prevent the GSF from carrying out its mandate and supporting the Haitian people."
feed.evidence: on the record, official statement; 3 photos
feed.other: Reported by EFE (Diario Libre), La Prensa Gráfica and Diario El Mundo; relayed by Radio Télé Confiance and Rolfy Martínez.

feed.who: Radio X Inter (@radioXinter), station in Gonaïves
feed.text: Says 33 new armored vehicles that arrived at Toussaint Louverture airport on Friday 23 Oct have been handed out, 20 to the GSF and 13 to the Haitian police, with the US Embassy facilitating, as the US strengthens both forces.
feed.evidence: 1 photo; no named source; not yet reported by others

feed.who: Vant Bèf Info (@vantbefinfo), Haitian outlet, reporter Moïse François
feed.text: Says the Haitian police ran a large operation on Sunday 25 Oct against the armed men occupying Bel-Air, and a police source says several gang members were killed, with no official toll. The same source says kamikaze drones were used against men "regularly involved" in kidnappings for ransom. Also reports clashes, heavy gunfire and drone strikes in Croix-des-Bouquets on Sunday.
feed.evidence: one police source, not named; 1 photo
feed.other: Le Médiateur (25 Oct) says the operation began around 5 p.m. with nearly five drones carrying explosives, and no official toll. EFE, citing Radio Télé Galaxie, also says several were killed.

feed.who: VWA-ZILE, relayed by Haiti Information Project (@HaitiInfoProj)
feed.text: Heavy gunfire was heard on Sunday evening in the Plaine area; early reports link it to an operation by the force against the gangs, backed by the police, to recover the remains of the four soldiers.
feed.evidence: early reports, no named source

feed.who: Citizen report from Bel-Air / Kafou 3, posted by Haiti Information Project (@HaitiInfoProj)
feed.text: Gunfire in several places Sunday night, at Kafou 3 and Risen Maten, and drones deployed, with casualties reported from the drones. Says "Solo," second in command of the Bel-Air gang under "Pèse" (a soldier for Izo), was shot several times by police and taken to a woman's house because he could not go to a hospital; rumors say he died. Says several innocent people were wounded or killed where two gang members were hit by a drone.
feed.evidence: one resident, not named; not yet reported by others

feed.text: Says tension remains high in the Cul-de-Sac plain, where the Task Force launched several drones during violent clashes in Santo, Croix-des-Bouquets, the stronghold of 400 Mawozo. On Sunday night, forces in downtown Port-au-Prince carried out kamikaze drone strikes in Bel-Air, "known as a hotbed of kidnappings," followed by heavy fighting between Haitian police (PNH) special units and gang members. Its first information is that PNH special units also entered gang-held parts of the commune of Mirebalais. It says it has no casualty figures yet.
feed.evidence: station's own reporting; 1 photo; no named source
feed.other: Not yet reported by others.

feed.who: Thériel Thélus ("TT"), Haitian journalist and founder of TripFoumi Enfo; posted in Creole and English by Haiti Information Project (@HaitiInfoProj)
feed.where: X, Haitian Creole with English translation
feed.text: Says security forces had already entered nearly 80 percent of Chen Mechan's strongholds in La Plaine but failed to hold the Damien area (the Faculty of Agronomy grounds), so the gang has regrouped. Says Chen Mechan's men have blocked the Croix-des-Missions bridge since Saturday night with large barricades, some with metal poles welded in place. Says the gang celebrated with gunfire and fireworks after attacking the Salvadorans, then came under heavy pressure when Bukele changed his tone; some fighters tried to move to other bases and many of their women fled to the provinces. Says the Chen Mechan leader has been hiding in Lizon since Friday, moving by motorcycle. Says a video circulating, reportedly from Chen Mechan, says they thought the Salvadorans' vehicle belonged to another group coming to kidnap, that the men inside fired first, that something in the car exploded, and that they then fetched water to put out the fire.
feed.evidence: named journalist; his sources not named; the Chen Mechan video he describes has not been seen by us
feed.other: Another source says: Radio Télé Confiance (25 Oct) says the Chen Mechan leader is dug in at Marin 12. The Chen Mechan video is not yet reported by others.

feed.who: The New York Times (updated story), in Spanish on Infobae
feed.text: Doctors were examining burned remains found Saturday. Scott Reece, a former State Department security official whose US-funded medical evacuation group Hero Client Rescue recovered them, says it was called Saturday afternoon to collect them. A person briefed on the matter says the ID Bukele posted belonged to a Chadian GSF soldier who was wounded and lost it. No ransom demand has been made. Says local media reported the Salvadorans were killed and then burned by Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo.
feed.evidence: named source (Reece); three or four people close to the mission, not named
feed.other: Bukele says the remains are not his men.

feed.who: Wilson Joseph, "Lanmò San Jou," leader of 400 Mawozo; English transcript by Haiti Information Project (@HaitiInfoProj)
feed.text: In the transcript he calls himself "the son of Jean-Jacques Dessalines," says "a cornered snake will strike back," and says that even "under attack, losing ground every day," he is still there. On the Salvadorans: "If God gave me the chance... to capture four white men... They wouldn't get the chance to die in my house—I'd capture them alive! And then... negotiations would happen right on the table!" He ends by boasting of his wealth and diamonds.
feed.evidence: video, 2 minutes 13 seconds, gang leader on camera; transcript by HaitiInfoProj
feed.other: HaitiInfoProj adds that Chérizier said the day before that the four were already killed.

feed.text: Posts a longer version of the new Lanmò San Jou video, dubbed into Spanish, with a Spanish text he calls a "direct threat" to Bukele. In his version Lanmò holds a bottle he calls "the bottle of papa Jean-Jacques Dessalines," calls to "shoot all the whites in Haiti," shouts "Bukele!", and says he could send 350 men with 350 long rifles and then return to the negotiating table. Three men seated beside him speak: they blame the Haitian state and "the whites, the politicians" rather than armed men for the country's troubles, and one says he is a police officer.
feed.evidence: video, about 10 minutes, dubbed; translation by the poster
feed.other: Another source says: Lepatrimoine509 (22:34) says the three men are people he says are police officers held hostage in his area. HaitiInfoProj's English transcript of a shorter cut does not include the call to shoot foreigners.

feed.text: Says that on his TikTok account Lanmò San Jou says the four Salvadoran soldiers died in Chen Mechan's stronghold in Santo, and that he presented three men he says are police officers held hostage in his area.
feed.evidence: relays the gang leader's video; no other source
feed.other: Dominican and Salvadoran accounts (Rolfy Martínez, @kapulet, @Noticia_Libre) report the same video the same way: he blames Chen Mechan and says he would have negotiated with Bukele.

feed.who: Wilson Joseph, "Lanmò San Jou," on TikTok (account @plip_plip_400, display name "lanmò_sanjou"); relayed on X by Rolfy Martínez (@RolfyMartinez) at 23:19
feed.where: TikTok, Haitian Creole video, about 99,000 plays; Rolfy Martínez's X relay about 500,000 views
feed.text: New video addressed to Bukele. Rolfy Martínez sums it up: the four Salvadorans died "by mistake," and if they had entered his territory he would never have killed them but would have negotiated with Bukele. @jaccelsalvador (22:12) first posted the TikTok link on X and asked for a translation.
feed.evidence: video, 5 minutes 36 seconds, gang leader on camera; we opened the TikTok page but did not watch it

feed.who: Korir Sing'oei, Principal Secretary for Foreign Affairs of Kenya (@SingoeiAKorir)
feed.text: "Deeply concerned at the deterioration of security situation in Haiti and the danger this poses to the Gang Suppression Force personnel. We stand in solidarity with the GSF." Quotes the GSF statement.
feed.evidence: on the record, signed post

feed.who: Nayib Bukele, President of El Salvador (@nayibbukele)
feed.text: "Thanks for the clarification. A little reading comprehension next time wouldn't hurt." Quotes Haití en Español (@haitienespanol, 16:29), which wrote: "We want to correct that President Nayib Bukele did not say that the soldier whose ID card he showed was dead. We apologize." Bukele had reposted that correction at 18:14.
feed.evidence: on the record, signed post
feed.other: Haití en Español's first post (13:51, about 956,000 views) showed a video of the soldier saying he is alive and said Bukele had said he died.
links: Haití en Español, first post with video

feed.text: Says Lanmò San Jou and Jeff Gwo Lwa have taken refuge in the commune of Saut-d'Eau since Wednesday, and the Chen Mechan leader is dug in at Marin 12, while their foot soldiers barricade their areas. In Shada both bridges have been blocked since Saturday with old tires and tree trunks, and armed men stop motorcyclists; Santo 11 has been paralyzed by barricades since Saturday. "The gangs are holding civilians in these areas to use them as human shields."
feed.evidence: station's own reporting; 2 photos; no named source
feed.other: Planet News (@ht_planet) relayed it in Creole. Another source says: Thériel Thélus (26 Oct) says the Chen Mechan leader is in Lizon.

feed.text: Reports the GSF statement and Bukele's denial side by side: the remains were handed over at Toussaint Louverture airport; Hero Client Rescue, led by former State Department security official Scott Reece and funded by the US, recovered them; doctors are examining them. Quotes GSF special representative Jack Christofides: "our thoughts are with the families of four missing personnel, their fellow soldiers, and the Government and the people of El Salvador."
feed.evidence: named officials quoted; GSF statement

feed.text: Posts a video he says Lanmò San Jou put out "at this very moment," showing his men of all ranks lined up in a Haitian street, saying he is guarding his people against "the enemy," which Martínez calls "the united forces of Haiti and El Salvador."
feed.evidence: video, 25 seconds; no date or place shown that we can check

feed.text: Seventeen days after the UN Panel of Experts report, the Dominican government has still not explained how Dominican Army (ERD) ammunition made in 2022 reached Haitian gangs. The report says "most" of about 900,000 rounds diverted from Dominican police stocks in 2024 went to 400 Mawozo and other groups in Port-au-Prince. The Defense Ministry says no transfer was authorized; Foreign Minister Ito Bisonó says the rounds date from the Trujillo era, but the report also cites rounds the Dominican authorities said they bought in 2022 from a maker in Colombia. A companion story (13:04) puts the value of the diverted police ammunition at over 92 million pesos and names the officers charged in Operation Pandora.
feed.evidence: UN Panel of Experts report, named officials
links: Listín Diario, value of the ammunition

feed.who: Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, speaking to reporters in Santiago; reported by Diario Libre
feed.text: Says the Dominican Republic has sent two more battalions, heavy equipment and artillery to the southern border, on top of about 11,000 men already deployed, and that he will meet the defense and foreign ministers and speak to Bukele again on Monday. "We have over-reinforced the southern border." The presidency says he will address the Haiti crisis on his weekly program on Monday 26 Oct at 3 p.m. Dominican time (21:00 Israel time).
feed.evidence: on the record, named official

feed.text: Says the Chadian soldier Sossal Kamis Alhadj, whose ID Bukele posted, is not dead but was wounded during operations this week, and that identification of the remains continues, including by dental records.
feed.evidence: 1 photo; no named source

feed.text: New headline: "Gang-fighting force in Haiti can't yet say if remains belong to four missing Salvadorans." Reports the remains came with two military badges and a shirt and were badly burned, with mixed-up body parts. Says a Chadian soldier said in a video that no Chadian had been killed, and that the force numbers over 2,000 troops from six countries.
feed.evidence: named reporter; GSF statement; a soldier on video
feed.other: Another source says: EFE puts the force at more than 1,000 soldiers.

feed.where: X, English, about 97,500 views; full statement as a photo
feed.text: "The #GSF confirms that it has received, through a third-party humanitarian organization, remains suspected of being those of the four personnel from the Salvadoran contingent currently missing. At this stage, the GSF is not in a position to confirm that the remains are those of the missing personnel." The full statement says the Chadian ID card Bukele posted belongs to a GSF soldier of the Chadian contingent: "The card was lost while conducting search operations for the missing Salvadoran personnel... The soldier is accounted for, present with his unit, and is not among the missing." It adds that coordination between Haitian security forces and the GSF remains essential.
feed.evidence: on the record, official statement; photo of the full text
feed.other: Le Nouvelliste, La Prensa Gráfica, El Diario de Hoy, BBC Mundo and EFE reported it; BBC Mundo headlined it as contradicting Bukele. Jake Johnston shared it at 15:03.
links: El Diario de Hoy, from EFE

feed.who: Jake Johnston (@JakobJohnston), Haiti analyst at CEPR, author of "Aid State"
feed.text: "According to @Ayibopost, the GSF soldier whose ID was posted by Bukele tonight is still alive, though he was injured during recent operations." Quotes AyiboPost: "It is not clear why the Salvadoran president disclosed his identifiable data." At 05:23 he added: "I can't imagine the GSF is thrilled about this."
feed.evidence: cites AyiboPost by name

feed.text: "The soldier published by Bukele is not dead." Says Sossal Kamis Alhadj was wounded but is alive, and that the GSF has received human remains it is working to identify.
feed.evidence: outlet's own reporting; sources not named in the part we could read (the article page loads its text by script, so we read only its summary)

feed.who: Nayib Bukele, President of El Salvador (@nayibbukele)
feed.text: "They are not our men." Says an NGO handed over human remains at the airport, saying they belonged to the four aviation technicians, but the remains are of a child, a man much taller than the technicians, and a person wearing part of the uniform of an army that is not El Salvador's; identity cards and military uniforms of other countries were also found among the remains. salvador: 26 to 27 Oct: the flights continue. The Miami Herald counts at least a dozen since Thursday, two on Sunday and cargo flights on Monday. Figures differ by source: 450 by Saturday "with hundreds more expected" (Herald), more than 500 special forces (Washington Post), at least 1,000 may ultimately deploy (Jake Johnston, no source given).

A separate command: Johnston (no source) and the Miami Herald ("reportedly") say Bukele wants some Salvadoran troops to operate outside the GSF, answering to his own commander in Haiti. Johnston: "A multilateral force, a bilateral force, and a private force."

The remains: a person familiar with the matter told the Washington Post it is "fairly certain" at least some are not the Salvadorans'; roughly three bodies were "almost fused together," and DNA testing is being done outside Haiti. Bukele has posted nothing on X since Sunday night, and Diario El Mundo says his government has given no new information nine days on.

How the four ended up there: Diario El Mundo says they used Google Maps to reach a supermarket and entered a gang area by mistake (no source named); the Washington Post says they "apparently lost their way"; analyst Romain Le Cour (El País) asks why four soldiers were in an unescorted vehicle in a gang-held area.
A video shared about 138,000 times as Bukele's commandos raiding a gang house in Haiti is from Ecuador, according to César Moreno; the posting account gave no source.

Dominican Republic, 26 Oct: Abinader says he backs Bukele, would receive him, and "will not allow those gangs within 20 kilometers of the border"; he says Haitian authorities themselves do not know the four's status. The foreign ministry says a post that had Bukele attacking the Dominican government is fake.

Remains, 25 Oct: the Gang Suppression Force says it received, through a humanitarian group, remains "suspected" to be the four, but "is not in a position to confirm" it. Bukele says they are not his men. The remains, recovered by the US-funded group Hero Client Rescue (Scott Reece), came with two military badges and a shirt and were badly burned (Miami Herald, Haitian Times). Vant Bèf Info says identification continues using dental records.

The Chadian ID: Bukele posted a Chadian GSF soldier's ID as found among the remains. The GSF says the card was lost during the search and the soldier is with his unit; AyiboPost and Vant Bèf Info name him as Sossal Kamis Alhadj and say he was wounded but is alive. After Haití en Español wrote that Bukele had called the soldier dead and then corrected itself, Bukele answered: "A little reading comprehension next time wouldn't hurt." Jake Johnston: "I can't imagine the GSF is thrilled about this."

Lanmò San Jou's 25 Oct TikTok video says the four died in Chen Mechan's area "by mistake" and that he would have taken them alive and negotiated with Bukele (Rolfy Martínez, Le Patrimoine 509). The New York Times says local media reported Chen Mechan and 400 Mawozo killed and burned them; no ransom demand has been made.

Four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with the Gang Suppression Force went missing on 18 Oct 2026 after their armored vehicle was attacked in Santo, Croix-des-Bouquets (Haitian Times; Salvadoran military via AP). Bukele says they are medical-evacuation personnel, not combatants.
On 21 Oct Bukele announced a military operation to rescue them and warned the gangs in Haitian Creole that he could "finish" them as he did in El Salvador.

Remains: on 24 Oct a group called HERO handed burned remains, collected at a drop site in Chen Mechan territory, to the Gang Suppression Force, while saying it was "in no way claiming it is them" (Jacqueline Charles, Miami Herald). The New York Times (Frances Robles) reported bodies "believed to be" the four. Bukele: "They are not our men"; he says the remains are a child, a much taller man and someone in part of another army's uniform, with other countries' ID cards and uniforms. Jake Johnston notes there is no official confirmation and the remains need an autopsy.

First combat: Franklin Vargas reports the first clash in the Cul-de-Sac plain with at least one Salvadoran wounded; Latinar says four were wounded. El Demócrata reports fighting against 400 Mawozo in Croix-des-Bouquets.

Troop numbers differ by source; see the reference table at the bottom of the page. Johnston, from flight listings, counted charter flights from Washington and from El Salvador into Haiti on 23 October, one likely a US Air Force plane.

Law: El Salvador's Special Transitory Law for the participation of its armed forces in the Gang Suppression Force was approved 29 Sep, published 30 Sep, in force 2 Oct 2026, and authorizes participation until Oct 2027 (Diario El Mundo, El Salvador).

Equipment: Armapedia's and Premium Media's photos show Yagu armored vehicles loaded onto a US C-130J at Comalapa; Menoni's and Premium Media's videos show armored vehicles at Las Américas airport in the Dominican Republic, which Premium Media says are bound for Port-au-Prince. Rolfy Martínez posted video he says shows "P50 tanks" in Port-au-Prince (not yet reported by others).

Dominican Republic: President Luis Abinader says he spoke with Bukele about logistical and intelligence cooperation against the gangs, and that he has reinforced the border with soldiers, armored vehicles, drones and aircraft. Listín Diario's reporter in Jimaní saw an army contingent arrive while the Mal Paso crossing stayed open.

On 25 Oct Abinader said two more battalions, heavy equipment and artillery have gone to the southern border, on top of about 11,000 men (Diario Libre). Listín Diario says the government has still not explained how Dominican army and police ammunition reached 400 Mawozo and other gangs, as the UN Panel of Experts reported.
gsf: 26 Oct statement: "Pressure on criminal groups will continue, and their acts of violence will not prevent the GSF from carrying out its mandate." EFE describes the photos: a convoy of eleven armored vehicles, Chadian soldiers, and a soldier in a Salvadoran helmet flying over the capital.

Size, per Dominican Foreign Minister Víctor "Ito" Bisonó (26 Oct): about 2,181 international personnel deployed, with a goal of about 5,500 within three months. The Dominican Republic gives the force logistics (transit, medical evacuations, air permits, blood, military cargo) but takes no direct part in operations.

Operations, 26 Oct: Salvadoran troops under the GSF and Haitian police ran a joint operation in Bon Repos (Miami Herald); Rolfy Martínez reports police and GSF offensives in Marin and Lizon and posts video of armored vehicles in Kenscoff; residents tell him the GSF presence in Croix-des-Bouquets is heavy.
PassBlue says the US plan for the GSF is not going well; Johnston: "Hard to imagine Bukele is going to undermine the GSF unless he's coordinating with at least some in USG."

25 Oct statement: received remains through "a third-party humanitarian organization"; cannot yet say they are the missing Salvadorans; the Chadian ID card belongs to a living GSF soldier; coordination with Haitian security forces "remains essential." Special representative Jack Christofides sent condolences to the families and to El Salvador (Haitian Times, EFE).
Size: over 2,000 troops from six countries (Miami Herald); another source (EFE) says more than 1,000, from El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mongolia, Sri Lanka and Chad.
Kenya's foreign affairs principal secretary, Korir Sing'oei, says he is "deeply concerned" at the danger to GSF personnel: "We stand in solidarity with the GSF."

The Gang Suppression Force (GSF) is the UN-authorized force under Security Council resolution 2793 (2025). Its mandate was renewed in September 2026 for six months, through March 2027 (Haitian Times).

Its commander is Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri (Haitian Times). Contributing countries named by Haïti Liberté: Chad, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mongolia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The UN calls it severely understrength; EFE says it has about 2,000 of a planned 5,500 from six countries.
In July a GSF patrol in Tabarre came under fire near an illegal checkpoint in Kraze Baryè territory; the GSF said three armed men were killed (Haitian Times, 19 Oct).
haitian: Bel-Air, Sunday night 25 Oct: a police operation that began around 5 p.m. used explosive drones (Le Médiateur says nearly five). Police sources tell Vant Bèf Info, Radio Télé Galaxie (via EFE) and HaitiInfoProj that several gang members were killed; no official toll. A resident (via HaitiInfoProj) says a local second in command called "Solo" was shot, and that innocent people were hurt by a drone strike.
The police posted video of its BRI unit on the ground in Mirebalais (27 Oct).
The Haitian army (FAd'H) tested about 2,000 recruits on Sunday for 700 places, part of a plan to recruit 15,000 in three years (EFE).
The Court of Appeal sent businessman Marc Antoine Acra and four others to trial without a jury in the 2015 Manzanares drug case (Radio Télé Confiance).

The Haitian Network of Anti-Corruption Journalists (RHAJAC) accuses Prime Minister Fils-Aimé of a quiet deal with gang leaders and asks for independent inquiries into who funds the gangs; it gives no evidence (Rezo Nodwes, EFE). In Gonaïves, the group COMOGINDA plans protests from November demanding operations against the gangs (Radio Tandans).
Jake Johnston and Vant Bèf Info: the Haitian government still has said nothing publicly. Dominican Defense Minister Fernández Onofre says the gangs control at least 70 percent of Port-au-Prince.

Sunday night, 25 Oct: forces in downtown Port-au-Prince carried out kamikaze drone strikes in Bel-Air, followed by fighting between PNH special units and gangs; PNH special units also entered gang-held parts of Mirebalais (Radio Télé Confiance, no casualty figures; not yet reported by others). The PNH posted video of its work to restore security in Petite Rivière de l'Artibonite.

Gangs are blocking roads in the Cul-de-Sac plain: both bridges at Shada and parts of Santo 11 since Saturday, with civilians held as human shields (Radio Télé Confiance); the Croix-des-Missions bridge since Saturday night, with welded metal poles (Thériel Thélus).
Thélus says forces had entered nearly 80 percent of Chen Mechan's strongholds but did not hold the Damien area, so the gang has regrouped.

The Haitian National Police say an offensive began 18 Oct in the Cul-de-Sac plain, in Croix-des-Missions, Santo, Carrefour Marassa and the Dyo and Las Vegas corridors, with many gang members killed and no count given (EFE via Diario El Mundo).
El Demócrata (Dominican outlet) reports Haitian police and the international force operating in Butte Boyer and Cité Doudoune on 24 Oct.
Retired Col. Himmler Rébu, a former Haitian army special forces commander, told EFE the Salvadorans "will not get results" because they do not know Haiti's ground, history and politics.
Haiti's government has called the soldiers' release a priority and says it is coordinating with the GSF (Haitian Times).
Haiti's government postponed the elections planned for December indefinitely in early October (EFE via France 24).
us: Radio X Inter (Gonaïves) says 33 armored vehicles that arrived on 23 Oct went 20 to the GSF and 13 to the Haitian police, with the US Embassy facilitating; not yet reported by others. El País says three of the first six aircraft to land were American.
No new statement found on 26 Oct from the State Department or the US mission to the UN; a US Embassy post that day carried only a photo and a link, which we did not open.

The group that recovered the remains, Hero Client Rescue, is a US-funded medical evacuation service led by Scott Reece, a former State Department security official (New York Times, Haitian Times). No new US government statement was found on 25 Oct; the State Department did not answer the Miami Herald about US transport for Salvadoran troops.
Ambassador Mike Waltz briefed the UN Security Council on 19 Oct and the US mission publicly told gang bosses the GSF "is coming for you."

Pimentel says Bukele was in Washington on 22 to 23 Oct to meet Trump and is asking for satellite intelligence, drones, armed helicopters and UN permission for offensive force. We have not found an official readout; the White House gallery page for a Trump-Bukele meeting that we opened is dated July 2025.

Jake Johnston (24 Oct) says the US military is giving logistical support to the Salvadoran deployment, and calls it "not a 'rescue' operation" but the US "again outsourcing to El Salvador… This is an end around." Premium Media's photos show Salvadoran armored vehicles loaded on a US C-130J.
The US designated Viv Ansanm and Gran Grif as terrorist organizations on 2 May 2025 (State Department).
contractors: Bel-Air, 25 Oct: a police source says the Task Force used drones against gang positions (HaitiInfoProj); Vant Bèf Info says kamikaze drones were used against kidnappers. A resident says innocent people were wounded or killed by a drone.

26 Oct: X posts repeat that Erik Prince's drones and a $52 million contract are part of the fight, with no source; Rezo Nodwes criticized the prime minister over the same $52 million contract. Nothing new from Vectus Global was found.

25 to 26 Oct: Radio Télé Confiance says the Task Force launched several drones during heavy clashes in Santo, Croix-des-Bouquets, and that kamikaze drones struck Bel-Air on Sunday night. A Spanish-language account (@erickprometeom) says the Task Force with Vectus Global is fighting alongside the international force for the first time; it gives no source.

Haiti's government created a Task Force that uses armed drones and helicopters against gangs and is supported by private contractors from Vectus Global, the company of Erik Prince (AP and Human Rights Watch).

Human Rights Watch (10 Mar 2026): Haitian security forces and private contractors working with them carried out drone strikes; at least 1,243 people were killed in 141 operations between 1 Mar 2025 and 21 Jan 2026, including at least 43 adults reportedly not gang members and 17 children; 738 were injured.

Vectus Global's contract was reportedly extended by one year at an additional $52 million, with operations expanded into Bas-Artibonite (Le Placentin, 10 Oct 2026, and other reports; we have not seen the contract). Reuters reported in Aug 2025 that Prince planned to keep personnel in Haiti for 10 years; OPB reported nearly 200 personnel.
Jake Johnston (CEPR) wrote on 23 Oct: "Bukele and Erik Prince seem to be in charge of the ongoing military operations." That is his judgment; he gave no source for it.

Jake Johnston wrote on 24 Oct that on paper the Salvadoran troops are under the Gang Suppression Force, but on the ground they join the Prince "task force," which is "staffed mainly with Salvadorans." Not yet reported by others.
Haïti Liberté (Kim Ives) uses the word "mercenaries" for GSF members; that is the author's word, not ours.

gangs: The coalition of the main Port-au-Prince gangs, formed in 2024 per El País (one source dates it September 2023). Jimmy "Barbecue" Chérizier is a leading figure and its spokesman. Designated a terrorist organization by the US on 2 May 2025. The Miami Herald's analyst says it had been fragmenting, and that this incident may restore its cohesion.

Led by Wilson Joseph, "Lanmò San Jou," operating in Croix-des-Bouquets and part of Viv Ansanm. He posted a video of ammunition and challenged Bukele (Anadolu). On 24 Oct new video showed him in a pickup with ammunition saying "We have to fight just to stay alive" (via HaitiInfoProj). On 25 Oct a TikTok video blamed Chen Mechan for the four Salvadorans' deaths and said he would have taken them alive and negotiated with Bukele; a longer version shows three men he says are police held in his area (Le Patrimoine 509) and, in César Moreno's Spanish version, a call to shoot foreigners. Radio Télé Confiance says he and Jeff Gwo Lwa have been in Saut-d'Eau since Wednesday. Listín Diario, citing the UN Panel of Experts, says most of 900,000 rounds diverted from Dominican police stocks went to 400 Mawozo and other groups. El Demócrata reports fighting against the gang in Croix-des-Bouquets. On 26 Oct he posted video singing and showing diamond teeth (Rolfy Martínez), and he says in a video that he holds three Haitian police officers; Herald sources say 400 Mawozo backed Chen Mechan's gunmen in the 18 Oct attack. His 25 Oct TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@plip_plip_400/video/7700668419598732558

Part of Viv Ansanm. Haïti Liberté, relaying Chérizier, says its fighters ambushed the GSF members in Santo; Lanmò San Jou now says the four died in its area. Salazar names Claude Celestin as its head. Martínez says its base was destroyed (not yet reported by others). The burned remains handed over on 24 Oct were collected at a drop site in its territory (Miami Herald). Radio Télé Confiance says its leader is dug in at Marin 12; another source, Thériel Thélus, says he is hiding in Lizon and moving by motorcycle, that the gang has regrouped and blocked the Croix-des-Missions bridge, and that a video attributed to it says the Salvadorans fired first and that its men tried to put out the fire (not yet reported by others). On 26 Oct César Moreno, citing one local, named former deputy Lemaire Pierre as the man arming the gang to control 34 neighborhoods (not yet reported by others); police and GSF offensives were reported in Marin and Lizon.

Downtown Port-au-Prince; Radio Télé Confiance calls Bel-Air a hotbed of kidnappings. Hit by police drone strikes on 25 Oct. A resident says its second in command, "Solo," under "Pèse," a soldier for Izo, was shot (HaitiInfoProj; not yet reported by others).
Controls territory in Tabarre where a GSF patrol came under fire in July (Haitian Times).
Gran Grif, Kokorat San Ras and Canaan

From March 2026 they attacked dozens of localities in the lower Artibonite; Gran Grif was designated a terrorist group by the US with Viv Ansanm (UN Panel of Experts report, hosted on HaitiDocs, and State Department).
Named by the Miami Herald's analyst as one of two leaders who spoke publicly this week.
